subject: Follow-up: Procurement readiness & AP blocker log — action items
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dana Morris <dana.morris@novaprod.com>, Gabe Johnson <gabe.johnson@novaprod.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Procurement readiness & AP blocker log — action items

Hi Dana / Gabe,

Thanks again for the time earlier — quick recap from our discovery and the concrete next steps so we keep procurement momentum moving. High-level notes from the call:  
- Procurement preference: PO-based invoicing looks likely, but there may be a short-term need to use card for proof-of-concept spend.
- AP constraints mentioned: vendor card monthly cap, vendor packet requirements (W9, bank details, insurance), and an internal legal review for any non-standard MSA terms.
- Marketplace: you asked whether Redwood is available via cloud marketplace (faster billing) as a fallback if PO timing slips.

Action items / asks (please confirm who owns each):
1) Dana/Gabe: confirm preferred payment path (PO vs corporate card for initial month) and target date to provide vendor packet (W9, bank remit, COI).
2) Soojin/Aditya: share our vendor onboarding questionnaire and MSA draft + sample invoice format (attached).
3) Marissa: schedule a short onboarding/checklist call once vendor packet is in — will collect SSO and integration contacts.
4) Finance: if you prefer marketplace, let us know and we can outline the difference (faster turn-up, marketplace fee ~5%).

I attached a quick procurement questionnaire and our onboarding checklist to make it easier to route through AP. If PO is the path, can you share your PO template so we can validate invoice fields in advance?

Proposed next meeting: 30 minutes the week of Apr 12 to align on timeline and outstanding documents — does Tue 4/13 or Thu 4/15 work?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0172

Attachments: Nova_Procurement_Questionnaire.xlsx (spreadsheet), Redwood_Onboarding_Checklist.pdf (PDF)

From: Dana Morris <dana.morris@novaprod.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Gabe Johnson <gabe.johnson@novaprod.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Apr 2027 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Procurement readiness & AP blocker log — action items

Soojin,

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from AP/Finance side:  
- Payment preference: Our standard is PO for third-party SaaS. Corporate card is only allowed for ad-hoc vendors and is subject to a $5,000/month per-vendor limit. For anything above that, we need a PO.
- Net terms: Standard is Net30, but Net45/Net60 are possible with approval from procurement leadership.
- Vendor packet: must include W9, bank remit details, a certificate of insurance (if the contract involves hosting), and completed vendor setup form — we aim to complete vendor onboarding in ~3–4 weeks once we have all docs.
- Marketplace: we can use our cloud marketplace for faster provisioning, but finance treats marketplace charges differently and they go through a procurement reconciliation process; there is typically a small fee.

We can commit to starting the vendor packet this week if Redwood can provide the W9-equivalent, MSA, and sample invoice fields. Gabe and I will loop in legal if we see any non-standard commercial terms.

Dana Morris
Director, Procurement
NovaProductivity
dana.morris@novaprod.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Procurement readiness & AP blocker log — action items

Hi Dana / Gabe — appreciate the details and quick turnaround. Two quick items from our side:  
1) Redwood can accept PO billing; we typically invoice Net30. We can accommodate Net45 on a case-by-case basis (will require approvals but we can route that through our finance ops).
2) If speed is critical, we do offer marketplace billing (Cloud Marketplace) which removes vendor packet overhead and can enable billing within 48–72 hours; it does come with a marketplace processing fee (~5%).

I've attached a short vendor packet we usually send and a sample invoice template to ensure your AP has the fields it needs (PO number, remit-to, line-item breakdown). If you can share your PO template and any specific invoice field constraints we will validate immediately.

Propose a 20-minute call Thu 4/15 at 10:00 AM PT to walk through the vendor packet and confirm the PO timeline — happy to invite finance/legal from our side if helpful.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
